requirement: Tool results MUST use the SDK’s `[REDACTED:<kind>]` marker for credential-shaped text under {cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`.
rationale:
The requirement says tool results MUST use the `[REDACTED:<kind>]` marker for credential-shaped text. Two marked tests cover this.

- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_excerpts_redact_credentials_before_serialization_and_paging]` writes a file with a GitHub token and a multi-line RSA private key. It runs the `search_text` and `search_structure` tools. It asserts that the excerpt equals the exact expected text. That text has `[REDACTED:GitHub Token]` and `[REDACTED:Private Key Block]` markers, with the surrounding text and line count preserved. It also asserts that neither the raw token nor any key body line appears in the serialized result. This covers two different kinds and two tools.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[queued_contents_and_graph_read_tools_redact_credentials_before_delivery]` covers the `read_node` tool result and the queued contents. It asserts that the chat history sent to the model has no raw token and does contain `[REDACTED:GitHub Token]`. The source shown to me had the raw token literal replaced by the marker, so `secret` and the marker string look identical here. In the real file, `secret` is the raw token. The dependency fingerprint is also asserted to hold the original text, so redaction only affects what is delivered.

Together these exercise the marker format for the credential-shaped cases the requirement names, across search and read tool results. The detailed matching rules, such as entropy extension and line-break preservation, belong to `requirements.authoring.redaction` and are tested separately (`crates/trust-but-verify/src/redaction/tests.rs`). I found no unacknowledged gap.

text: Tool results MUST use the SDK’s `[REDACTED:<kind>]` marker for credential-shaped text under {cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`.
Habeas MUST apply the SDK's built-in credential rules to source text supplied
in mandatory inputs, tool reads, and search results, and to source text shown
in the book and `habeas info`. The same rules apply to configuration files.
Each match of a built-in `secretshape` rule MUST be replaced with
`[REDACTED:<rule name>]`, preserving every line break. The match MUST extend
through adjacent regions flagged by the entropy heuristic when only whitespace
separates them. Entropy alone MUST NOT trigger a replacement.
Outlines MUST use the original source for structure and spans. Structural
hashes MUST use the redacted text for each matched region as specified in
pinned exactly because changes to its rules can affect evidence hashes.
